title: Global Perspective and Epidemiology of COVID-19

questions.question: Name 4 groups who were included in the NACI recommendations for phase 1 Vaccination in December 2020 for COVID-19.

parts.text: Name 4 groups who were included in the NACI recommendations for phase 1 Vaccination in December 2020 for COVID-19.

questions.model_answer: NACI's December 2020 initial (Phase 1) key populations for COVID-19 vaccination: (1) residents and staff of congregate living settings that provide care for seniors (e.g., long-term care facilities/nursing homes), (2) adults 70 years of age and older (with priority increasing with age), (3) health care workers with direct patient contact (including those in long-term care), (4) adults in Indigenous communities where infection can have disproportionate consequences.
questions.beyond_mandell: NACI (National Advisory Committee on Immunization, Canada) preliminary guidance on key populations for early COVID-19 immunization, December 2020; this specific recommendation is not covered in the Mandell immunization chapter text.

parts.text: Give three reasons that SARS-CoV-2 has evolved into a worldwide pandemic and MERS-CoV did not.

questions.model_answer: 3 reasons SARS-CoV-2 caused a pandemic while MERS-CoV did not: (1) SARS-CoV-2 achieves substantial transmission from pre-symptomatic and asymptomatic/mildly symptomatic individuals, allowing silent widespread community spread, whereas MERS-CoV transmission occurred predominantly from symptomatic, often severely ill patients, making case identification and containment easier; (2) SARS-CoV-2 binds ACE2 receptors that are abundant in the upper respiratory tract, favoring efficient respiratory droplet/aerosol transmission between casual contacts, whereas MERS-CoV's DPP4 receptor is more predominant in the lower respiratory tract, requiring closer/prolonged contact for transmission and resulting in lower overall transmissibility (lower R0); (3) MERS-CoV had a geographically limited zoonotic reservoir and exposure route (dromedary camels concentrated in the Arabian Peninsula), limiting global spread, whereas SARS-CoV-2 spread efficiently and rapidly worldwide via international travel before containment measures could be implemented.
questions.beyond_mandell: Comparative epidemiology of SARS-CoV-2 vs MERS-CoV - pagefile unavailable for this chapter (null).
